external_entities.name: insurance partner
external_entities.description: One of three insurance partners that provides a daily extract.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Three insurance partners drop a daily extract for us.
external_entities.notes: The source does not identify the three partners individually.

external_entities.name: analyst
external_entities.description: An analyst who queries the warehouse directly.
external_entities.notes: The source describes analysts collectively and does not identify individual analysts.

processes.name: Airflow scheduler
processes.description: A scheduler that runs nightly at 02:00, lists and reads files from the landing bucket, and triggers a Spark transform job for each file.
processes.source_excerpt: An Airflow scheduler running in the landing network wakes up at 02:00, lists the bucket, and reads whatever is there.
processes.notes: The scheduler has access to connection strings and partner keys stored in its metadata database. It does not check that a file came from the partner whose folder it landed in.

processes.name: Spark transform job
processes.description: A transform job triggered for each file that normalizes records and loads them into BigQuery.
processes.source_excerpt: For each file the scheduler triggers a Spark transform job in the warehouse network.
processes.notes: Nothing validates the row contents beyond the schema.

data_stores.name: landing bucket
data_stores.description: A bucket receiving daily claim-record extracts from the insurance partners.
data_stores.source_excerpt: They push files into a landing bucket over SFTP.
data_stores.notes: I don't know how the landing bucket is encrypted. Both are on defaults as far as I know.

data_stores.name: Airflow metadata database
data_stores.description: Airflow's metadata database, which stores connection strings and partner keys.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Airflow keeps its connection strings and the partner keys in its own metadata database.
data_stores.notes: I don't know ... whether the Airflow metadata database is encrypted at rest. Both are on defaults as far as I know.

data_stores.name: BigQuery
data_stores.description: The warehouse containing normalized claim records queried directly by analysts.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The transform normalizes the records and loads them into BigQuery.
data_stores.notes: Analysts have a dataset-wide grant and member-identifying columns have not been split out.

data_flows.name: drop files
data_flows.description: An insurance partner pushes a daily extract into the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: They push files into a landing bucket over SFTP.
data_flows.notes: Each partner has a static key issued when they onboarded; the keys have not changed since.
data_flows.data_description: Claim records with member names and dates of birth

data_flows.name: read files
data_flows.description: The Airflow scheduler lists and reads files from the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: lists the bucket, and reads whatever is there
data_flows.notes: The source does not state how the scheduler authenticates to the bucket or how the connection is protected.

data_flows.name: store credentials
data_flows.description: Airflow stores connection strings and partner keys in its metadata database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Airflow keeps its connection strings and the partner keys in its own metadata database.
data_flows.notes: The source does not state the database connection protocol or authentication mechanism.

data_flows.name: trigger transform
data_flows.description: The Airflow scheduler triggers a Spark transform job for each file.
data_flows.source_excerpt: For each file the scheduler triggers a Spark transform job
data_flows.notes: The source does not state the protocol, authentication, encryption, or data exchanged for triggering the job.

data_flows.name: load records
data_flows.description: The Spark transform job loads normalized claim records into BigQuery.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The transform normalizes the records and loads them into BigQuery.
data_flows.notes: Nothing validates the row contents beyond the schema.
data_flows.data_description: Normalized claim records with member names and dates of birth

data_flows.name: query warehouse
data_flows.description: An analyst queries the warehouse directly.
data_flows.notes: Analysts authenticate with SSO and have a dataset-wide grant; member-identifying columns have not been split out.

trust_boundaries.name: landing network
trust_boundaries.description: The network in which the Airflow scheduler runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: An Airflow scheduler running in the landing network

trust_boundaries.name: warehouse network
trust_boundaries.description: The network in which the Spark transform job runs and analysts are located.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The transform job in the warehouse network
trust_boundaries.notes: Analysts are also stated to be on the warehouse network.

assumptions.assumption: The claim records in the landing bucket are confidential.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the extracts contain claim records with member names and dates of birth; disclosure of member-identifying data harms individuals.

assumptions.assumption: The connection strings and partner keys in the Airflow metadata database are confidential.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the database stores connection strings and partner keys, which are credentials and secrets.

assumptions.assumption: The normalized claim records in BigQuery are confidential.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the transform loads claim records containing member-identifying data into BigQuery.
